correctness.rationale: Euclidean division z=qm+r gives z in <m,m+1> iff q>=r. Thus for 0<=j<m, j² is a gap iff (j² mod m)/m > [m/(m+1)](j/m)². Completion by differencing yields |sum_j e((hj+kj²)/m)|²<=m gcd(2k,m)<=2|k|m, valid for composite as well as prime moduli, with k=0,h nonzero geometric sums zero. Two-dimensional Erdős–Turán–Koksma gives D*<<m^(-1/3) log(2m) at H=floor m^(1/3), and K=ceil m^(1/6) monotone strips produce O(m^(5/6) log m) uniform in u,v. Replacing m/(m+1)x² by x² changes main term <1. Independent small-modulus exact counts checked membership and approximate 2/3 trend; not proof of limit.
residual_risks: Uniform statement is over fixed u,v endpoints and all m; it does not yield nontrivial control on intervals shorter than its error scale.

value.rationale: A natural enumeration problem for all square gaps in the classical two-consecutive-generator numerical semigroup, providing its previously undetermined asymptotic root distribution and a uniform power-saving interval estimate. The limit is mass 2/3 rather than a normalized probability law; precise counting profile can be used in further semigroup-square statistics.
residual_risks: No generality to arbitrary pairs of generators or higher powers.

final_claim: Uniform all-modulus root-profile estimate G_m(u,v)=m integral_u^v (1-t^2)dt+O(m^(5/6) log(2m)), in particular 2m/3 square gaps of <m,m+1>.
limitations: Density 1-t^2 is an unnormalized counting measure of total mass 2/3; 0<=u<=v<=1; all m>=2. Finite counts do not establish the asymptotic.
